about: How people keep in touch in a past year (Back when, companion/world_year.py). A world that runs in a past year in a modern city gets one chat line from the span its year falls in. Each line names only what was already around at the start of its span, so nothing from a later year reaches the chat.

spans.line: Most homes have a landline and an answering machine; pagers are common, and only a few people carry a mobile phone, a big one used for calls. People keep in touch by calling, leaving messages, writing letters and cards, and making plans in person. Almost nobody texts or has email at home.

The landline at home and the answering machine are still how most people call; pagers are common and more people carry a mobile phone, mostly for calls. Email and dial-up internet are new at home, and people meet in chat rooms. Texting is rare, and plans are made by phone or in person.

Most adults carry a small mobile phone with buttons and text in short bursts, pressing a key several times for each letter, though calls are still the main thing; every home has a landline. People email, and chat on AIM, MSN Messenger or ICQ at a computer at home.

Everyone has a mobile phone, mostly flip phones and sliders with a small camera, and texting on the number keys is how people keep in touch day to day; a BlackBerry means work. People chat on AIM or MSN Messenger and keep a MySpace page, and students are on Facebook.

Most people carry a flip phone, a slider or a BlackBerry and text all day; touchscreen smartphones are new and still a treat. Friends keep up on Facebook and MySpace, chat on MSN or AIM, and share photos by uploading them from a digital camera.

Smartphones are taking over (iPhone, Android, BlackBerry), though plenty of people still have a flip phone. People text, keep up on Facebook, follow friends on Twitter and snap photos on their phones; video calls are on Skype.

Almost everyone has a smartphone. People text and keep group chats on WhatsApp, iMessage or Facebook Messenger, post photos on Instagram and Facebook, send Snapchats, and video call on FaceTime or Skype.
Everyone lives on their smartphone: group chats on WhatsApp, iMessage or Messenger, Instagram posts and stories, Snapchat, voice notes, and FaceTime or video calls in the evening.
Everyone lives on their smartphone: group chats, Instagram stories, short videos on TikTok, voice notes, and video calls with friends and family.
Everyone lives on their smartphone: group chats, Instagram and TikTok, voice notes, and video calls with friends and family.
